ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a single-loop biased diode circuit: on the left is a small-signal sinusoidal voltage source labeled 5 sin(ωt) mV, in series with a DC bias voltage V; at the top is a diode; on the right is a 100 Ω resistor; the bottom node is grounded. Therefore, for the small signal, in the path driven by the sinusoidal source, the diode's small-signal impedance is in series with the 100 Ω resistor. Reasoning: The given DC diode current I_D = 26 μA, ideality factor n = 1, thermal voltage V_T = 26 mV, so the diode small-signal conductance g_d = I_D/(nV_T) = 26 μA / 26 mV = 0.001 S = 1 mS. Junction capacitance C_j = 0.5 nF, ω = 2×10^6 rad/s, so the capacitive admittance jωC_j = j(2×10^6)(0.5×10^-9) = j0.001 S. The diode small-signal admittance Y_d = 0.001 + j0.001 S, therefore the diode small-signal impedance Z_d = 1/Y_d = 500 - j500 Ω. After being in series with the 100 Ω resistor in the figure, the total impedance Z_total = 100 + Z_d = 600 - j500 Ω, whose magnitude |Z_total| = sqrt(600^2 + 500^2) = sqrt(610000) ≈ 781.0 Ω. The small-signal source amplitude is 5 mV, therefore the diode current small-signal amplitude |I| = 5 mV / 781.0 Ω ≈ 6.40 μA, taken to one decimal place as 6.4 μA.

Apply KCL at that node: v_x/100 = Y_d(v_s - v_x). Solve v_x = [100Y_d/(1 + 100Y_d)]v_s. Reasoning: The given DC diode current I_D = 26 μA, ideality factor n = 1, thermal voltage V_T = 26 mV, so the diode small-signal conductance g_d = I_D/(nV_T) = 26 μA / 26 mV = 0.001 S = 1 mS. Junction capacitance C_j = 0.5 nF, ω = 2×10^6 rad/s, so the capacitive admittance jωC_j = j(2×10^6)(0.5×10^-9) = j0.001 S. The diode small-signal admittance Y_d = 0.001 + j0.001 S, therefore the diode small-signal impedance Z_d = 1/Y_d = 500 - j500 Ω. After being in series with the 100 Ω resistor in the figure, the total impedance Z_total = 100 + Z_d = 600 - j500 Ω, whose magnitude |Z_total| = sqrt(600^2 + 500^2) = sqrt(610000) ≈ 781.0 Ω. The small-signal source amplitude is 5 mV, therefore the diode current small-signal amplitude |I| = 5 mV / 781.0 Ω ≈ 6.40 μA, taken to one decimal place as 6.4 μA.
